title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
lede: The weights stay frozen. Watch a question find its evidence — embed, score, keep the nearest three, answer from them.

audience.who: engineers who have called an LLM API and heard the word RAG
audience.leaves_knowing: knowledge lives in the index, not the weights — update the shelf, not the model

critique_of_obvious: The usual RAG diagram is three boxes and two arrows. It never shows why chunk c1 beats chunk c2, so the viewer cannot tell retrieval from magic.
mechanism: A language model only knows what was baked into its weights at training time. RAG adds a second, swappable memory at inference time: the question is embedded into a vector, every document chunk has been pre-embedded into the same space, and the chunks are scored by cosine similarity. The top-k nearest are pasted into the prompt as context, and the model generates an answer grounded in them, usually with citations back to the source chunk.

anchor.what: a shelf of five document chunks across the top, with the query pill entering from the left

c1.text: Returns accepted within 30 days of delivery.

c3.text: Refunds are issued to the original payment method within 30 days.

c4.text: Our warranty covers manufacturing defects for 1 year.

worked_example.derivation: cos(q,d) = (q·d) / (|q||d|) for every chunk; sort descending; keep k = 3. Work c1 in full on screen: dot product term by term, both magnitudes, the quotient.
worked_example.abstraction_note: 4-D illustrative embeddings, labelled on screen as a projection of a real 1536-D space (text-embedding-3-small).

beats.label: The question
beats.caption: A question arrives. The model alone can only guess from whatever was frozen into its weights.
beats.idea: Without retrieval the model answers from frozen training data.
beats.focal_motion: the five chunks stagger onto the shelf; the query pill slides in from the left

beats.label: Embed everything
beats.caption: Query and every chunk become vectors in one shared space. Same space, or nothing can be compared.
beats.idea: Query and chunks are embedded into the same vector space.
beats.focal_motion: each chunk unrolls into a four-cell strip beneath it; the query does the same

beats.label: Cosine similarity
beats.caption: Similarity is the cosine of the angle between two vectors. Work c1 in full: dot product over magnitudes.
beats.idea: Cosine similarity scores the query against each chunk.
beats.focal_motion: the c1 arithmetic types itself out term by term in the detail band

beats.label: Keep the top k
beats.caption: Sort by score. Keep the three nearest. The shipping and support chunks fall away.
beats.idea: Only the k highest-scoring chunks survive.
beats.focal_motion: score bars grow under each chunk; the two lowest dim to the ground

beats.label: Build the context
beats.caption: The three survivors are pasted into the prompt beside the question. That prompt is all the model sees.
beats.idea: Retrieved chunks are inserted into the prompt as context.
beats.focal_motion: the three chunks slide down into a prompt box beneath the question

beats.label: Grounded answer
beats.caption: The model reads question plus context and writes the answer from what it was handed: thirty days.
beats.idea: Generation is conditioned on the retrieved context.
beats.focal_motion: the answer streams out character by character in the detail band

beats.label: Cite the source
beats.caption: Every claim points back to the chunk it came from. Provenance is free when retrieval is explicit.
beats.idea: Each answer span is traceable to a source chunk.
beats.focal_motion: a thread draws from the answer back up to c1 and c3 on the shelf

beats.label: Why it matters
beats.caption: Knowledge lives in the index, not the weights. Swap the shelf and the same model answers from today's documents.
beats.idea: Retrieval is a memory you can edit without retraining.
beats.focal_motion: the shelf re-lights and one chunk swaps out; the answer thread re-attaches

aha: The model's weights stay frozen. You change what it knows by changing what you retrieve, so the same model answers from today's documents, cites its sources, and hallucinates less. Retrieval is a memory you can edit.

refs.title: Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Karpukhin et al., Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

claims.text: The model's parameters do not change at inference time; retrieval changes the context, not the weights.
Query and passages are embedded into one shared dense vector space so they can be compared.
Passages are ranked by vector similarity and the top-k are kept.
The generator conditions on the retrieved passages and can attribute its answer to them.
